review: The hymn is the charge to a servant: 1:1–3 is Rom 12:1 with Phil 3:12, 2:1–6 is 2 Tim 4:5 with John 15:20 (the thorny way) and Luke 11:13, and 3:1–6 is 1 Cor 6:19–20 with Rom 6:11 and 2 Tim 2:4.
Stanza 1 prints three lines and stanzas 2–3 six each (3/6/6), the print's `12.12.12.12.12.12 – 8.8.8.6`; the payload keeps the short opening as the consecration before the charge.

2:3–4 keep the two sayings of the Lord as two parallel lines beginning וְאָמַרְתָּ, following the print's twice-repeated وَقُلْتَ لِي; the colon of 2:3 is the glossary's device for the quoted speech, and the second line needs none because it continues the same report.
3:1 uses פִּקָּדוֹן, the deposit-word of Lev 5:21–23, for the Arabic أَمَانَة, so the body and spirit are something held in trust rather than owned.
